text: No surviving mortal, midwayer, or seraphim may ascend to Paradise, attain the Father, and be mustered into the Corps of the Finality without having passed through that sublime experience of achieving parental relationship to an evolving child of the worlds or some other experience analogous and equivalent thereto. The relationship of child and parent is fundamental to the essential concept of the Universal Father and his universe children. Therefore does such an experience become indispensable to the experiential training of all ascenders.

All mortal survivors who have not experienced parenthood on the evolutionary worlds must also obtain this necessary training while sojourning in the homes of the Jerusem Material Sons and as parental associates of these superb fathers and mothers.

ch18.s3.u1.k: The midwayers are permanent inhabitants who remain on the planet, linking the changing seraphic administrations.
ch18.s3.u1.p: The first permanent citizens met on the ascending journey are the midwayers of our own planet. The seraphim come and go with their assignments, but the midwayers remain. They are at once natives of the planet and ministers, preserving continuity amid changing administrations. The memory and responsibility of a world are entrusted to those who stay there.

text: Midwayers may be regarded as the first group of the permanent inhabitants to be found on the various orders of worlds throughout the universes in contrast with evolutionary ascenders like the mortal creatures and the angelic hosts. Such permanent citizens are encountered at various points in the Paradise ascent.

Unlike the various orders of celestial beings who are assigned to minister on a planet, the midwayers live on an inhabited world. The seraphim come and go, but the midway creatures remain and will remain, albeit they are nonetheless ministers for being natives of the planet, and they provide the one continuing regime which harmonizes and connects the changing administrations of the seraphic hosts.

ch18.s3.u2.k: As citizens of Urantia the midwayers work persistently for its progress and keep growing in wisdom and experience.
ch18.s3.u2.p: The midwayers have a kinship interest in the destiny of this planet. Though brought into existence fully developed, they never cease to grow in wisdom and experience, and they possess a genuine evolutionary culture. That unseen cousins living on the same world are working with us for the progress of our civilization reminds us that mankind is not alone.

text: As actual citizens of Urantia, the midwayers have a kinship interest in the destiny of this sphere. They are a determined association, persistently working for the progress of their native planet.

While the midwayers were brought into existence fully developed—experiencing no period of growth or development from immaturity—they never cease to grow in wisdom and experience. Like mortals they are evolutionary creatures, and they have a culture which is a bona fide evolutionary attainment.

ch18.s3.u3.k: The generations of men forget, but the midwayers remember, and their memory is the treasure house of planetary tradition.
ch18.s3.u3.p: Human generations forget, but the midwayers, the immortal citizens of this planet, remember. Through their memory the culture of a planet remains ever present. That the life and teachings of Jesus have been restored to us through the midwayers shows well the worth of the memory of those who remain.

text: The generations of men forget; the corps of midwayers remembers, and that memory is the treasure house of the traditions of your inhabited world. Thus does the culture of a planet remain ever present on that planet, and in proper circumstances such treasured memories of past events are made available, even as the story of the life and teachings of Jesus has been given by the midwayers of Urantia to their cousins in the flesh.

ch18.s4: The Survival Plan and the Humblest Citizens
ch18.s4.u1.k: The whole universe organization is devoted to the survival plan of bringing God down to man and carrying man up to God.
ch18.s4.u1.p: High spirits, angels, and midwayers stand in different places but serve the same purpose: to bring God down to man and, in partnership, to carry man up to God. And this plan is open not only to mortals but to midwayers as well. Even the abiding citizens at last share in the great current of ascent.

text: The entire organization of high spirits, angelic hosts, and midway fellows is enthusiastically devoted to the furtherance of the Paradise plan for the progressive ascension and perfection attainment of evolutionary mortals, one of the supernal businesses of the universe—the superb survival plan of bringing God down to man and then, by a sublime sort of partnership, carrying man up to God and on to eternity of service and divinity of attainment—alike for mortal and midwayer.

ch18.s4.u2.k: The spornagia are unique creatures without personality whose identity persists, and they may someday reach a higher destiny.
ch18.s4.u2.p: The spornagia who tend the architectural worlds of the system capital do not respond to the adjutants of worship and wisdom and so have no surviving soul. Yet the experiential identity formed by their five-adjutant mind persists. And there is hope that someday they may rise from the animal level to spiritual achievement. The care of the universe is not closed even to its humblest creatures.

text: Spornagia are the only creatures in all the universe of Nebadon who experience this or any other sort of reincarnation. They are only reactive to the first five of the adjutant mind-spirits; they are not responsive to the spirits of worship and wisdom. But the five-adjutant mind equivalates to a totality or sixth reality level, and it is this factor which persists as an experiential identity.

There are those who believe that, in a future universe age, these faithful spornagia will escape from their animal level of existence and attain a worthy evolutional destiny of progressive intellectual growth and even spiritual achievement.

ch18.qs1: Between moving on and remaining, how is faithfully keeping my present place connected with my own growth?
ch18.qs2: If the experience of parenthood is essential to knowing God as Father, what am I learning through caring for someone else?
ch18.qs3: What part can I take in preserving the memory and traditions of my community?
